title: Secrisk correlation handoff and secrets inventory sync
content:
Context:
Quick sync to hand off the risk-correlation work from vuln-pipeline experiments into the main triage flow, and to coordinate the secrets inventory pilot before the platform-wide rotations in Q1. This is a working note — outcomes and action items below.

Attendees: Priya, Evan, Lina, Marcus, Yuki (+ notes from on-call rota: Alex via slack)

Agenda:
- Review correlation algorithm prototype and false-positive profile
- Decide handoff timeline and rollout gating for vuln triage
- Secrets inventory pilot plan: scope, tooling, owners
- Threat-modeling tabletop scheduling & deliverables
- Runbook and alert tuning follow-ups

Summary / Decisions made:
1) Correlation rules: adopt fingerprint+repo+path bucketing as default for the triage queue.
   - Rationale: prototype reduced duplicate triage items by ~68% during October test window and preserved unique findings for active branches.
   - Implementation: add the rule as a non-blocking pre-filter in pipeline v2 for 2-week canary; after successful canary, flip to default.
   - Ticket: JIRA:SEC-542 created for rollout and canary monitoring.

2) Severity mapping refinement: map "secrets-detection" hits to P1 only if (confidence>=0.85) AND (token-type in [aws, gcp, hmac]) OR (exposure path == ci/cd). Otherwise mark P2.
   - Why: too many medium-confidence hits from historical commits were creating noise. This improves TTR for real incidents.

3) Secrets inventory pilot: scope limited to repos under "infrastructure/" and "deploy-scripts/" for initial run. Use detect-secrets + runtime trufflehog scan for historical commits.
   - Expected volume: trufflehog raw hits ~1.2k across the two repo groups; after heuristics and entropy filters expect ~120-160 actionable items.
   - Ticket: JIRA:SEC-543 for running pilot and generating the secrets-matrix artifact.

4) Rotations & remediation: rotate any confirmed credential in inventory older than 180 days or with unknown owner. Platform-engineering to handle AWS key rotation; product teams handle SDK tokens.
   - Ticket for coordination: JIRA:SEC-544 (rotation coordination & automation checklist).

5) Threat-modeling tabletop: schedule Dec 6 with Solutions Eng + Platform Eng to walk through attack paths found by the correlation prototype. Deliverable: prioritized list of 5 mitigations and a decision log.

Discussion notes / highlights:
- Evan: correlation reduced duplicate noise but we saw a small class of false merges where distinct secrets in different contexts shared a short fingerprint. Agreed to append repo/path to fingerprint to reduce collisions.
- Lina: flagged that detect-secrets baseline must be refreshed before the pilot to avoid historical credentials causing churn. Tasked Lina + Marcus to produce baseline snapshot.
- Marcus: proposed integrating KMS key metadata (rotation date, owner tag) into the secrets-matrix to speed up triage; platform-eng will expose a read-only endpoint for the pilot. Action: Marcus to file infra PR (see linked PR for infra changes).
- Yuki: asked about CI noise — agreed to add a suppression rule for strings found only within test fixture directories and third_party vendored code.

Open questions / unresolved items:
- What threshold for "unknown owner" triggers SOC escalation vs. product owner contact? (Tentative: 72 hrs auto-escalation to SOC after two owner contact attempts).
- How do we handle service principal keys embedded in Helm templates? Flag as high-confidence but add a Helm-specific reviewer path.
- Confirm expected billing impact of additional trufflehog historical scans (platform-eng to provide estimate).

Action items (owner — due):
- SEC-542: instrument canary for correlation rule, add monitoring dashboards (Evan) — due 2026-12-07
- SEC-543: run secrets inventory pilot for infra repos, produce secrets-matrix artifact (Lina, Marcus) — due 2026-12-04
- SEC-544: produce rotation runbook and stake-holder contact list (Priya + Platform Eng liaison) — due 2026-12-10
- Baseline refresh: capture detect-secrets baseline snapshot and store in Confluence (Lina) — due 2026-11-30 (in-flight)
- Infra endpoint for KMS metadata: expose read-only list for pilot (Marcus) — PR opened: linked PR — review by 2026-12-02
- Threat-modeling tabletop prep: collate scenarios and attacker profiles (Yuki + Solutions Eng) — due 2026-12-03

Runbook / Monitoring changes to be made:
- Add a dashboard tile for "correlation-filtered items" vs. "raw findings" to track false-negative risk.
- Add a scheduled weekly job (cron) to re-run trufflehog on infra repos with S3-backed artifact retention for 30 days.
- Alert tuning: secrets-detection alerts to include confidence score and discovery path to speed triage.

Notes on risk prioritization:
- Prioritize keys exposed in CI/CD and production config over dev/test fixtures.
- Treat keys with high-privilege (root-like or admin) as P0 for immediate rotation.
- Low-confidence historical hits should be assigned to a backlog remediation lane for batching.

Next steps / meetings:
- Dec 6: Threat-modeling tabletop (Solutions Eng + Platform Eng) — invite has been sent.
- Weekly sync: continue Thursday 09:30am for rollout updates until canary stable.

References & artifacts:
- Confluence: secrets-matrix-2026 (work-in-progress)
- GitHub PR: infrastructure changes for KMS metadata endpoint (see linked PR)
- JIRA tickets: SEC-542, SEC-543, SEC-544 (created during this meeting)

Notes to self (informal):
- Watch for sudden spike in correlation-filtered items after canary starts — likely indicator of a mis-tuned canonicalization rule.
- Keep a short list of temporary suppression patterns — but avoid long-lived suppressions without post-mortem.

Meeting adjourned.
